producer_report.summary: The athena.toml exempt entry for 39962ed, its explaining comment, and the CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] Fixed entry were already present in the working copy. I re-read all three and confirmed them against each criterion. No further edits were needed. Only athena.toml and CHANGELOG.md are modified. cargo test --locked and cargo clippy passed. The history check cannot exercise 39962ed in this one-commit snapshot; it reports only the snapshot's own root commit.

checks_run.note: Exit 0 with no error reported; the first lines show 38 tests in athena_agent passing. The output was too large to tail, so the per-binary totals were not read, but no failure was reported.
Finished with no warnings or errors.

Ran with --bin because plain cargo run is ambiguous (athena and xtask binaries). It reports one violation on commit bc31fa13d920, the snapshot's own root commit. The snapshot has one commit, so 39962ed is not in it and this check cannot exercise the new exempt entry here. The failure is not about 39962ed.
Shows only CHANGELOG.md and athena.toml modified.

criteria_check.evidence: Read athena.toml line 152: exempt = ["49c6ac15...", "64ecdc9a...", "ee4b0dd1...", "f2a8453380...", "5a734782...", "39962ed02fec9da2d87cd4a3e287121ed229cd0f"]. Six entries: the five existing ones are unchanged, and the full 40-character id is appended last. The entry was already in the working copy when I resumed; I re-read it to confirm it.

criteria_check.criterion: A comment above exempt explains the entry for a maintainer: the squash of PR #130 carried jobs 20261010-154004-60r4 (PR #129 closed unmerged) and 20261017-121143-sg0j, so the chain between them is broken and neither landing is valid in that commit; same remedy as ee4b0dd (D66) and f2a8453 (D70).
criteria_check.evidence: athena.toml lines 147-151 (the comment directly above exempt) say the squash of PR #130 carried 20261010-154004-60r4 (PR #129 closed unmerged) and 20261017-121143-sg0j, that the chain between them is broken so the history check finds neither landing valid, and that it is excused as ee4b0dd (D66) and f2a8453 (D70) were.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] has an entry saying 39962ed is exempted from the history check and why.
criteria_check.evidence: CHANGELOG.md lines 60-66, under ## [Unreleased] > ### Fixed: the entry names 39962ed, the squash of PR #130, the two jobs and the broken chain, and says it is added to [history] exempt with the same remedy as ee4b0dd (D66) and f2a8453 (D70).

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test and cargo clippy: both pass, so the config still parses and any config-validating tests accept the new entry. Run cargo run -- check --history if available; it should no longer fail on 39962ed (records may be absent in the snapshot).

The history check ran as cargo run --locked --bin athena -- check --history (plain cargo run is ambiguous between athena and xtask). It reports one violation on the snapshot's root commit bc31fa13d920, not on 39962ed, because the snapshot has a single commit and does not contain 39962ed. The check cannot exercise the new entry in this snapshot.

open_issues: The history check cannot be run against 39962ed in this snapshot, so the claim that it no longer fails on 39962ed is not verified here. It is an unverified expectation based on the file change, not a measured result.
The snapshot's own root commit bc31fa13d920 fails `check --history`. This is an artifact of the snapshot having no real history, not part of this change.
mistakes: My previous report did not show criterion 1 as met, although the entry was already in athena.toml. I did not re-read the file to confirm it before reporting. This time I re-read it and cite the line.
learnings: athena.toml [history] exempt already had 39962ed appended, with its comment at lines 147-151, when this job resumed.
CHANGELOG.md already had the Fixed entry at lines 60-66 under [Unreleased].
The workspace has two binaries (athena and xtask), so plain `cargo run` needs --bin athena.
The snapshot's single root commit bc31fa13d920 is flagged by `check --history`. The snapshot contains no governed-content landing for it, so the check reports it.
desires: A way to run the history check against the real repository history, or a snapshot that includes 39962ed, so the new exempt entry can be exercised directly.
